She highlighted the impact of amendments to the State Constitution’s proposals which would result in millions of lost revenue to the City which she also indicated could impact the budget for some First Responders. She alleged that at a recent City of Sunrise meeting, they discussed taking a hardline approach in reducing “feel good” expenses due to the proposed property taxes.
MAYOR ARSERIO responded to Commissioner Simone and said that although he did not disagree about the taxes and that Margate would have to tighten their belts in certain areas, he did not believe the City would be out of pocket for this Item and that they could, in fact, gain some revenue.
Discussion ensued including the cost to the City and statistics.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS confirmed that it did not cost the City anything as it was revenue that was lost and said that the average amount of what customers spent was $8.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ spoke in favor of this Item and advised that it was something that cities did with their tax revenue and said that it could well be that a child who attends this facility with a parent would return. She had more concerns with the City’s policy for allowing the free use of the Margate Sports Complex as the staff would have to be paid for organizing the event.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS advised that the City collected a lot of permit revenue for the use of the Margate Sports Complex and that it was not rented out for free barring those that applied for fee waivers.
Discussion ensued.
MS. SANCHEZ thought it was a good idea for one child per family who had signed up for the program but she did not agree with siblings being included for free.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO responded to Ms. Sanchez’s comments and said that he did not have a problem with a child and their sibling as long as it was with two paying adults.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS highlighted the difficulties in determining whether it was a sibling or a friend and recommended that for ease of this initiative, he would ask that the City Commission keep it to one ticket.
Discussion ensued.

BROWARD COUNTY PROPERTY APPRAISER (BCPA) MARTY KIAR thought it would be important to provide an update on the property tax proposals in Tallahassee. He provided the background on this proposal and advised that the Florida Policy Institute organized a study to eliminate all property taxes and questioned how they could replace that lost revenue. He explained that after that proposal was rejected, the conversation changed from eliminating all property taxes to Homesteaded property taxes but advised that the State Governor would not have a veto and whatever was put on the ballot was through the House and Senate. He advised that the Senate had not come up with a plan and had some concerns about diminishing public services. He advised that currently, there were proposals moving through the Florida House of Representatives and that they were very concrete where there was a possibility that it could make it to the ballot. He advised that next week was Broward Days in Tallahassee 2026 and indicated that it was a good opportunity to discuss with those who were in the legislature about those impacts. He informed that the proposals did not affect the school portion of the tax bill, that they prohibited the reduction in funding for police and that they were starting to add amendments to prohibit the reduction for firefighters as well.
He provided a overview on the proposals on the Fiscal Impact Estimates for Broward County (BC) & Margate and his PowerPoint presentation discussed the following points:
HJR 201: Elimination of Non-School Property Tax for Homesteaded Properties
HJR 203: Phased Out Elimination of Non-School Property Tax for Homesteads
HJR 205: Elimination of Non-School Property Tax for Homesteaded Property for Persons Age 65 or Older
HJR 209: Property Insurance Relief Homestead Exemption of Non-School Property Tax
HJR 211: Accrued Save-Our-Homes Property
HJR 213: Modification of Limitations on Tax Benefit for Non-School Property Tax
COMMISSIONER, TOMMY RUZZANO, referenced residents’ taxes which were paid to the City and informed that the revenue of one third respectively went to the City, BC and the schools.
BCPA KIAR concluded his presentation and thanked the City for giving him the opportunity to provide his presentation.
A question and answer session ensued.
MAYOR ANTONIO V. ARSERIO thanked BCPA Kiar for all that he did and encouraged residents to sign up to Owner Alert. He advised the public to review all the policies and forewarned that the City could lose $14,500,000 if they eliminated taxes.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO questioned that if the Broward County Public School (BCPS) was the only tax collector, if they could get receivership of the property. He did not believe that half of the money that went to BC or the BCPS got represented well. He advised that for the last seven years, the City had not raised taxes which he voted against.
BCPA KIAR repeated that any proposal could only be applicable to Homestead property taxes and explained that the school portion of the bill was not impacted and that it would be treated like anything else. He explained that Margate was a very fiscally responsible City.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER, ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ, thanked BCPA Kiar for clarifying the things that were going up in Tallahassee. She preferred if they could lower homeowners insurance as a separate initiative.
Discussion ensued.

COMMISSIONER, ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ wished everyone a Happy New Year. She hoped that the public attended the first City Commission meeting to listen to the presentation by Broward County Property Appraiser (BCPA), Kiar and forewarned about giving up being homesteaded.
COMMISSIONER, JOANNE SIMONE, advised that today, the design concept for the Calypso Cove marquee digital sign was finalized and referenced that this had taken over a year. She informed that the Property Improvement Grant Program (PIP) would be rolled out again next February but voiced her concerns due to the uncertainty outlined in BCPA Kiar’s presentation pertaining to taxes. She requested City Manager Curtis to pause the PIP until they knew where they were with the taxes.
MAYOR, ANTONIO V. ARSERIO, asked the City Clerk to poll the City Commission pertaining to the roll out of the PIP.
CITY MANAGER, CALE CURTIS, confirmed that the City’s money would be utilized for the PIP and that they had not, as yet, advertised a start date for applications but would consider February.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ said that it was something that she could consider.
COMMISSIONER, TOMMY RUZZANO, explained that the City Commission was here to make the community look better and to help the residents. He received positive feedback from residents that said that the PIP was the best thing that the City had done. He believed that Margate would be sustainable despite what may come in front of them and asked the City Manager to review all the extra money that the City Commission receive apart from their pay. He had no problem with the grant.
Discussion ensued.
VICE MAYOR ANTHONY N. CAGGIANO would prefer the grant to be placed on hold until an update had been received from Tallahassee.
MAYOR ARSERIO preferred to see the grant continue and would also like to see an additional separate carve-out for Homeowners Associations (HOA).
CITY MANAGER CURTIS explained that they had $500,000 budgeted for PIP which commercial properties, HOAs and residential properties were eligible for.
MAYOR ARSERIO wanted to see the grant to continue in its current format.
Discussion ensued on the process of the PIP.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ confirmed that she did not have a problem with the City doing what they were going to do.
MAYOR ARSERIO informed the City Manager that he had CONSENSUS to proceed with the PIP.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE expressed that it was very disgraceful that one could not give their opinion without a personal attack. She apologized to the residents for allowing this to happen. She was all for helping the City and the residents but mindful not to spend dollars which they may not have in the future and that they needed to start saving money now. She wanted action on overgrown trees infringing on neighbors’ properties and did not believe that someone would have to incur a fee to do it and requested the City Manager to review and address it.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO apologized if he upset any of the City Commission and referenced freedom of speech. He advised that it would be the 250th anniversary of the United States this July. He wished everybody the best.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO explained to Margate residents that he was taking notes while they were speaking. He hoped that the rest of the year was a lot happier.

minutes_note:
CITY MANAGER CURTIS invited Department of Environmental and Engineering Services (DEES) Director, Keyser to give a brief presentation on this Item.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER, advised that this whole effort was being spearheaded by Broward County (BC). He introduced Director of Water & Wastewater Operations for BC, Mark Darmanin, who was available via Zoom. He explained that biosolids were the solid particles which were generated in the wastewater plant and after that process, it would eventually be spread on a farmer’s field.
A brief question and answer session ensued between DEES Director Keyser and the City Commission.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER continued to discuss the process and explained that there were many regulations that the land application sites had to adhere to. He advised that type B biosolids contained bacteria, pathogens and viruses and that they got down to a 16% water content or less. He explained that there were 60 total permitted sites where DEES could discharge it which were all above Tampa and Lake Okeechobee and advised that their outlets were shrinking but the number of producers were not and in effect, they were competing against each other for places to dispose the biosolids. He discussed in detail the biosolids regulatory timeline and the difficulties therein. He anticipated that DEES would eliminate the application of Class B biosolids which would require them to go to Class A or AA in order to land apply it and highlighted that there were a number of utilities in BC that were in the same boat which would create more competition.
A brief question and answer session ensued between DEES Director Keyser and the City Commission.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER forewarned that the costs to dispose of the biosolids would increase asymptotically which cost $461,000 in 2025. He explained that approximately five years ago, a BC representative spearheaded an effort with all of the producers in BC and advised that they could respectively deal with it independently or they could join forces together and configure how they can pull their resources and build one central plant that could deal with it for everybody which resulted in a group being placed together in 2021 to create a Biosolids Solutions Working Group. He forewarned that if the City was not proactive, it would continue to accelerate expeditiously. He advised that the group thought that the best location to place it would be in BC’s Water Waste Water Plant which was at the northwest corner of Copans Road and Powerline Road. He said that once it went through the process, it would produce ash and fertilizer which they could dispose of at the landfill without any environmental regulatory issues. He said that there were a number of options for the final destination including the possibility of selling it as fertilizer and if there was a market for that product, the revenue would be apportioned on the same percentage as the expenses.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ said that when methane gas came out from the plant on Copans Road, the public were displeased with the smell which was stopped after a while as they had to do something.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER did not believe that they would be producing methane gas but referenced it would be produced at the dump which they could use as a source of energy to drive this plant.
Discussion ensued.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER continued with his PowerPoint presentation and highlighted the thermal drying process that the working group recommended and said that DEES was looking at a 10,000 wet ton per year allocation. He approximated the sum of $200,000,000 - $570,000,000 to construct a plant in BC. He advised that the working group completed a Interlocal Agreement (ILA) study confirming the feasibility and that the next step would be to design a facility but he had doubts on the final number. He confirmed that the City’s participation would be 3.7% of $1,850,000 allocation or commitment to the design which would be their second ILA. He informed that the third ILA would pertain to the construction and the operation of the plan.
.
MAYOR ARSERIO was trying to reduce costs and suggested that there could be a possibility that they would not hit the estimated 10,000 tons as highlighted by DEES Director, Keyser, for another 20 - 30 years. He questioned if they could they lease it to any City and give them the extra three in exchange of something.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER highlighted that there was a performance criteria that they would have to meet with the product that was being sent but he was unsure if there would be any issue with the agreement or legalities but if they did what Mayor Arserio suggested, they could only do that temporarily.
CITY ATTORNEY TOLCES advised that it would probably be something that they would probably see later on in the operation agreement.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ voiced her concerns that it would cost $50,000,000 to design something and questioned that if cities joined thereafter, would they have to pay the $1,850,000. She expressed that it was a huge commitment of money during a period when they may have to worry about the future of property taxes.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER explained that pertaining to the $50,000,000, they would not get a good estimate from a consultant point. He said that they believe they have a reasonable construction cost and the consultant would seek approximately 10% but it was unrelated and that the strategy was to be conservatively high and manage expectations and the contracts. He was honest and they were looking for a reasonable solution to a very difficult situation and in terms of the costs, they had to start somewhere to move this Item ahead and read a list of the municipalities that had approved or were still considering the same.
Discussion ensued including what municipalities would be using the facility, apportionment costs and whether BC would use the facility or build something independently.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS advised that it was enterprise fund dollars and that it had been identified in the Capital Improvement Plan for the Waste Water Treatment Plant. He also informed that it had been identified as an eligible product in the Utility Revenue Bond that they just passed.
Discussion ensued.
MAYOR ARSERIO anticipated that the residents voted for them to improve their stormwater/wastewater treatment and this was an eligible expense within that bond which was something to consider.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER forewarned that there was one technicality that they had to explore before utilizing the bond money and referenced what would occur if it did not qualify.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS confirmed that this Item would definitely not be withdrawn from the General Fund budget.
DEES DIRECTOR KEYSER advised that BC wanted to know by the end of February whether they were in or out, for at least for the design. He suggested that they could participate in the design to see what the ILA, construction and operating agreement looked like. He personally did not anticipate that they were going to spend $1,850,000 to design it and then walk away and that everyone in BC had researched it.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO questioned whether BCs Darmanin knew what the City of Coconut Creek paid per year for their portion of the biosolids disposal. He voiced his concerns about the apportionment element of any potential agreement and also referenced the Alpha 250 property. He said that they needed a plan and was not enthused with partnering with BC.
Discussion ensued
DIRECTOR OF WATER & WASTEWATER OPERATIONS (W&WO) FOR BC, MARK DARMANIN, advised Commissioner Ruzzano that he did not have that number as it was not really separated. He explained that the collaborative group of cities that send their waste to BC’s regional facility for treatment purposes totaled 100,000 tons of biosolids per year which would be BC’s responsibility.
Discussion ensued including what the other cities were paying per year, exploring the project independently, partnering with BC, finding a suitable site for the facility, environmental issues, the language contained in the ILA and potential legal issues.
DEES ASSISTANT DIRECTOR, MARTA RECZKO clarified that if this Item cost around $500,000,000, BC would cover approximately 40% of the costs/ownership of this facility and going forward on the operational costs, Margate would cover 3.7%. She also clarified the current costs which Margate were paying.
Discussion ensued.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS advised that BC was looking for all of the participating cities to make a decision, sooner rather than later. He advised that if they have satisfied the City Commission’s questions or suggested ideas, they could take action and pass the Resolution and the ILA to move forward with the design or alternatively, they can revisit this Item at a later date if further research was required.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO expressed his reluctance to move forward and said that he would prefer to be the last participant to make this decision.

FIRE CHIEF, ROBERTO LORENZO, informed that the American Red Cross, representative, Mr. Ortega, would be providing a PowerPoint presentation.
AMERICAN RED CROSS, COMMUNITY DISASTER PROGRAM SPECIALIST, STEVEN ORTEGA, discussed the Home Fire Campaign initiative which pertained to making their community safer and more resilient in the face of a disaster such as a home fire. He explained that the program was designed to prevent deaths and injuries caused by home fires which accounts for more than 60,000 disasters which they respond to every year in the Red Cross. He explained that one of their objectives was to be invited into their communities and to be able provide the public with free smoke alarm installations as well as fire information on how to prevent any type of disaster from occurring in the home. He advised that they also provide bed shakers for the hard of hearing. He continued to discuss the importance of this program and the process of installing these devices by volunteers which included door to door installations and an educator.
FIRE CHIEF, ROBERTO LORENZO, continued to speak positively on this program and thanked the City’s Fire Marshal, David Scholl.

minutes_note:
MAYOR, ANTONIO V. ARSERIO, provided instructions on how to submit a Public Discussion.
MARGATE VOTER, MR. KRALJIC, commented about repositioning the camera for public speakers. He also requested that they should reinstate public comment over Zoom and the City’s social media accounts.
PRESIDENT OF MALLORY HARBOR HOA AND CHAIR OF THE COUNCIL OF ASSOCIATIONS AT CORAL BAY, FREDERICK T. BOURDIN, celebrated 30 years living in Margate and disagreed with some of the previous public speaker’s comments.
MARGATE RESIDENT who lived in Margate for approximately 25 years and was attending her first City Commission meeting. She alleged that comments she read on social media platforms and residents who she conversed with did not want another apartment in this City and referenced congestion. She praised the Margate Police Department.
MARGATE RESIDENT, DONNA L. FELLOWS, thanked the City Manager for the parking and for reviewing the crosswalk light between State Road 7 and Margate Boulevard. She also recommended that Margate needed established restaurants and referenced Flanigan’s, Hooters and LongHorn Steakhouse.
MARGATE RESIDENT, TRACY VAN WINKLE, thanked the City Manager and referenced the cleanout of Southgate Boulevard Plaza. She said that the City did not need any more apartments.
MARGATE RESIDENT, ELSA J. SANCHEZ, agreed with a previous comment pertaining to the availability of Zoom comments for the residents. She hoped that they would repeat First National Girls and Women’s Sports Day annually. She congratulated the Fire Department for receiving a contract with the City and also praised the Police Department and School Resource Officers for their wonderful program which helped the children.
MAYOR ARSERIO requested that Ms. Angier’s time be suspended as she had some very important information to share.
CONSENSUS was given by the City Commission.
THE NORTH BROWARD HOSPITAL DISTRICT (NBHD) BOARD OF COMMISSIONERS CHAIR AND MARGATE RESIDENT, STACY L. ANGIER, discussed a flyer pertaining to a backroom deal merger by Broward Hospitals which she said was bad news for the taxpayers. She read an op-ed that was published by a Community doctor who practiced at the Memorial which addressed some inaccuracies in an opinion essay written by Kelly Skidmore.
Discussion ensued.
TONY SPAVENTO, 3194 W. BUENA VISTA DRIVE, suggested that they should be building some kind of educational complex across the street and not more apartments and said that they wanted jobs.
MARGATE RESIDENT, DIANA PERMANAN, envisaged the City to have something more productive where they would give back to the community and concurred with other comments that they did not need more apartments. She was pleased to see Commissioner Simone as a board member.
RICHARD ZUCCHINI, LAKEWOOD ON THE GREEN, encouraged residents to attend more meetings where they would establish the facts and referenced the Live Local Act.
title: PUBLIC DISCUSSION
Anyone wishing to comment on any matter relating to City business or on any item on the Consent Agenda should approach the podium now. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.

minutes_note:
COMMISSIONER, ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ, discussed Homesteaded properties, referenced the hospital district and people voting against their own self interest. She voiced her concerns about property insurance.
MAYOR ARSERIO interjected and indicated that a third of Florida residents and voters were renters and forewarned that they would not benefit from this.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ highlighted the ever changing development that she had seen as a 44 year Margate resident. She did not do government by Facebook and explained that she voted against building anything that had to do with apartments and rezoning on either golf courses. She voted against Coconut Creek and Banks and referenced not receiving any monies for the same in comparison to others. She sent Easter and Passover greetings to those who practiced.
COMMISSIONER, JOANNE SIMONE, highlighted the forthcoming City events. She had spoken to several residents who would like to see the City Chambers' cameras positioned to the public speakers. She asked people to stay well and be safe.
COMMISSIONER TOMMY RUZZANO, said that the residents needed to know what was happening in the City. He believed that he was the most transparent and agreed with Commissioner Simone about repositioning the cameras which he previously requested. He read a post that he uploaded to Facebook and explained why residents were disgruntled and discussed the City Commission’s votes on apartments. He also highlighted issues with Code including those from residents.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ said that she had asked for a Workshop on Code.
MAYOR ARSERIO discussed issues with Code and suggested if the City experiment by taking a more relaxed approach and only address residential complaints or major violations.
Discussion ensued on Code and whether they should organize a Workshop.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO continued to detail his areas of concern in the City which included the area surrounding a disused BB&T building, Chevy Chase Plaza, the golf course and referenced changing the zoning. He discussed public safety and said that separating from Coconut Creek was the worst move and said that he had spoken to officials pertaining to a four-way merger. He referenced revenue initiatives and proposed using approximately three or four acres near Walmart and Lemon Tree Lake to build a beautiful townhome project and on Rock Island Road. He said that they have to create a happy work environment and referenced a four day work week. He said that they needed to be sensible about the downtown and explained that he could not park at the Promenade. He said that there was a broken tax system which needed to be adjusted. He forewarned that there could be a shortage of incoming funding and the City needed to be creative and forward-thinking and that he encouraged Facebook questions.
VICE MAYOR ANTHONY N. CAGGIANO sent Easter, Passover and Ramadan greetings and asked everyone to be safe and healthy.
MAYOR ARSERIO repeated his proposal of making use of the Florida Power & Light Company (FPL) easement and was aware that someone was considering utilizing it as a community parking area and potentially two nurseries who would lease some of that property which he said was a no brainer.
CITY MANAGER, CALE CURTIS, informed that if somebody was interested in utilizing that property, they could always submit a proposal to the City for review.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ said that from 1999, there was an entire picture of suggestions for the FPL easement which included garden projects and parks but she did not want to see an enclosed area on that green space parking. She liked the idea of community gardens and landscaping but said that the proposals would need to be for the community.
MAYOR ARSERIO thanked City Manager Curtis and referenced that the sidewalks in Pinewalk Drive’s south area had been repaired on both sides of the road and he was also impressed with the pressure cleaning from a third party contractor. He requested a child swing for Firefighters’ Park and recommended a consistent weekly equipment check due to feedback pertaining to squeaks and mold. He forewarned that the Live Local Act would affect probably the entire stretch of 441 and he discussed the same. He also referenced Senate Bill 180 (SB180) pertaining to hurricanes and advised both building and zoning restrictions would be suspended for seven years. He also advised that one website was saying from a national level, they were trying to make zoning and permitting easier as they were blaming the local cities and counties for restricting the development of homes and forewarned that as time moved, the local municipalities would have zero control and provided an example of a situation in Ft. Lauderdale.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS believed that the swing was on order.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO concurred with Mayor Arserio’s comments on the Live Local Act and proposed changes to zoning.
Discussion ensued.
title: COMMISSION COMMENTS

minutes_note:
There was no report.
CITY ATTORNEY, DAVID N. TOLCES, said that the bill Mayor Arserio was referring to was House Bill 979 which would be effective in the tri-county. He advised that this would affect properties that were in excess of five acres which could be next to residential development and that if the property had been designated as a brownfield or was otherwise contaminated and had been cleaned up through the state program.

He wished everybody a Happy Passover and Easter and highlighted the City’s Springtime Egg Hunt. He informed about the Margate Elementary School’s fundraiser. He also said that he would have no problem with any support for fire or police vehicle being used if they needed to share any resources. He voted “no” on the project for the downtown and said that he was uncomfortable with moving forward with too many units. He informed that the Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) board did not have the authority to put anything on the ballot and as the Mayor, he had no problem letting the residents decide and it would be discussed at the next City Commission meeting. He anticipated that there would be no issue of the Golf Course giving the City the clubhouse and wanted to see what the other resources were.
CITY MANAGER, CALE CURTIS, explained that there had been a variety of conversations with the respective developer for the property regarding that piece of land where McDivot’s was. He said that it would require restoration and he believed it was a great opportunity to attempt to obtain that as it was one of Margate’s landmarks. He said that financially, there were a number of options on how it could be operated such as renting the facility.
Discussion ensued.
MAYOR ARSERIO thanked Legacy Closet pertaining to the sponsorship from Texas Roadhouse. He said that the median enhancements had been going on along Rock Island Road and questioned whether funds had been exhausted. He referenced the Tree Giveaway and sponsors and requested an extra 50 trees for the staff to plant them around the City. He asked for an update on the house on Royal Palm Boulevard opposite Calypso Cove. He requested that the City stay on top of the fertilization and the weed and feed schedule for the newly landscaped medians.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS said that they were also looking at other areas of the City pertaining to median enhancements and that the City received a $100,000 reimbursement grant for the trees along Rock Island Road. He had been discussing with the Parks and Recreation Director on where to go to next with continuing to enhance and improve the City. He agreed for additional trees to improve landscaping around the City. He said that he would speak with City Attorney Tolces with a status update on the property on Royal Palm Boulevard and said that the intent with the support from the City Commission would be to work with an organization such was Habitat for Humanity to get them to reconstruct a house.
Discussion ensued on the property on Royal Palm Boulevard.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO complimented the improvements made on the medians along the stretch between Margate Boulevard and Royal Palm.

VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO explained a situation where a Code Officer asked Wendy’s to remove feather banners during a grand opening. He preferred to have a six month trial where they would allow feather signs in front of businesses on the weekend only.
MAYOR ARSERIO had no problem supporting businesses and implement some sort of action on this Item but would prefer for City Manager Curtis to return with two or three recommendations.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO explained that he asked for this Item to be placed on the Agenda as his neighbor received a code violation for having feather banners at their business site. He wanted to help businesses as far as he could and would probably look into it for plaza store owners but would refrain car dealerships. He suggested that Code Compliance should not enforce it until they devised something.
Discussion ensued.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS cautioned staying away from a moratorium as he informed that it had some challenges but he could commit to working diligently with staff and devising some amenable code amendments that would allow for those types of advertising signs that would be acceptable.
MARGATE RESIDENT, JASON MILLER, suggested some initiatives and said for a small business, they definitely needed the banners.
MARGATE RESIDENT, TABITHA MILLER, explained that at weekends, customers remarked that they were able to see their business on State Road 441 due to the display of signs but highlighted that many did not see the small shop owners in a plaza. She would appreciate if there was something that the City could implement to help them.
MS. CULVER said that not holding the property owners accountable was hurting the small businesses and explained that rotating the banners was not a good idea. She advised that something had to be done for the survival of the businesses.
Discussion ensued on the process of the Ordinance change.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE was 100% in favor of the feather banners but indicated that the City needed to devise a way of executing it tastefully. She highlighted a similar situation to the Millers where a shop owner got coded in the same plaza.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO recommended also looking at the monument signs on the properties.
MAYOR ARSERIO confirmed that there was CONSENSUS to come back with options.

minutes_note:
Item ID 2026-069 was heard before 4) City Manager's Report.
MAYOR ARSERIO explained why he asked for this Item to be placed on the Agenda which was previously discussed at a CRA meeting. He preferred to see either no apartments in the downtown or let the residents vote on a range. He asked the City Commission if there was CONSENSUS to place a ballot question and if so, he wanted to work at a quick pace on obtaining the same.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO thanked Mayor Arserio for placing this Item on the Agenda but thought that there was actually going to be a ballot question. He indicated that it would be difficult to devise or suggest a ballot question but said that they needed CONSENSUS to move forward with entertaining the same.
CITY ATTORNEY, DAVID N. TOLCES, explained that the City Commission would have to go through a two step process at this meeting which was whether they wanted a ballot question and if so, the next step would be the question of costs. He advised that he provided details in his memorandum.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS advised that to put the question on with the Supervisor of Election was approximately $106,000.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO assessed that there was a large number of people that did not want the apartments which he also was not a fan of. He explained the voting results at the Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) meeting and commented that the City Commission should honor the public and vote on it and suggest a question to place on the ballot.
Discussion ensued including the terms of a Special Exception.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ responded to Commissioner Ruzzano’s comments.
Discussion ensued.
CITY ATTORNEY TOLCES read an extract from the Section 163.3167(8) of the Florida Statutes and advised that it greatly limited the ability for citizens to vote on developments within a municipality or the County and advised that if there was an amendment to the code that the public wanted to see, it may not be able to be voted upon. He advised that this matter was valid and binding as both the CRA and the developer had signed the agreement. He informed that if the City was unable to reach an agreement or CONSENSUS with respect to the conceptual plan, then he believed that the CRA and the developer would be able to terminate the relationship.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ wanted clarification that the City Attorney just informed them that there was absolutely nothing the City could place on the ballot.
Discussion ensued including public development.

MAYOR ANTONIO V. ARSERIO, provided instructions on how to submit a Public Discussion.
MARGATE RESIDENT, STACIA MURRAY, commented on the maintenance of the Margate Executive Golf Course and said that they had stopped doing the irrigation with the water and that the pools had been ruined. She thanked the Building Code Services staff.
MARGATE RESIDENT, DONNA L. FELLOWS, queried about the engravement of bricks at the Dog Park.
CITY MANAGER, CALE CURTIS, advised Ms. Fellows that it was administered through their Parks and Recreation (P&R) Department.
MARGATE RESIDENT, ELSA J. SANCHEZ, thanked P&R for the wonderful job they were doing on Rock Island Road/Margate Boulevard. She discussed her experience of being a victim of fraud and thanked staff members in the Police Department.
MARGATE RESIDENT, JONATHAN KRALJIC, read a statement on the demolition of the basketball court at Centennial Park with the replacement of a pickleball/tennis court.
title: PUBLIC DISCUSSION
Anyone wishing to comment on any matter relating to City business or on any item on the Consent Agenda should approach the podium now. Each speaker is limited to three (3) minutes.

minutes_note:
COMMISSIONER, ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ, referenced a new phone and advised Ms. Sanchez to bring the device into the store. She sent a Happy Nurse’s week and Mother’s Day greetings. She discussed the construction at the Executive Golf Course.
COMMISSIONER, JOANNE SIMONE, congratulated Rise Academy who were recognized by the Education Insider Magazine for being the top STEAM (Science, Technology, Engineering, Arts, and Mathematics) School 2026. She referenced the National Nurses Week and said that May was also recognized as Haitian American Heritage Month. She congratulated the Employees for their Years of Service and referenced the Department of Environmental and Engineering Services (DEES) Cline and Purchasing Manager Shambray. She sent Happy Mother’s Day greetings.
COMMISSIONER TOMMY RUZZANO, sent Happy Mother’s Day greetings. He did not disagree with Mr. Kraljic’s view on the basketball court and questioned if the City could add a hoop.
CITY MANAGER, CALE CURTIS, responded to Commissioner Ruzzano and referenced time and money. He said that the City could get a price and see about adding a court but forewarned that it would cause a delay with the contractor.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO congratulated the Employees and discussed the success of the Tree Giveaway. He highlighted that the 4th July Parade was coming and wanted to make it bigger and better each year.
Discussion ensued on the procedure for the 4th July Parade and Fireworks during the Coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) pandemic.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO thanked everybody who was involved with the City’s School Resource Officers (SRO) and advised that for now, they rescinded their letter to take Margate’s Police Officers out of the schools.
VICE MAYOR ANTHONY N. CAGGIANO thanked Commissioner Simone for recognizing Haitian American Heritage Month and said that they were the very first country in the hemisphere to fight off slavery and highlighted The Sultane Cuisine & Bakery Restaurant. He sent Mother’s Day greetings and commented on the success of the Tree Giveaway.
MAYOR ARSERIO had no problem revisiting the basketball courts at Centennial Park but anticipated that the neighborhood would oppose it. He highlighted that there had been a lot of back and forth for a few years with several public meetings, emails, surveys, etc. and said that no one had ever come in to demand a basketball court. He believed that the City was one of the most accessible at City meetings and went above and beyond for allowing Public Comment on Agenda Items. He attended the Broward County School Board (BCSB) meeting and explained that he did not arrive in time to register to speak. He referenced 4th July and said that it was one of the City’s most well attended events throughout the year and indicated that there could be additional fireworks. He discussed the operational hours of the Calypso Cove Aquatic Facility and apologized that the pump for the kids splash area was closed due to a faulty pump. He discussed hurricane preparedness and referenced tax incentives. He highlighted that Panda Express was in the permit process of coming to Margate. He explained that Margate had changed to the 20th Congressional District which would no longer be represented by Congressman Jared Moskowitz and advised the public to do their research on candidates and the precincts. He pushed for median enhancements at their last budget meeting which he described as a well funded project and he provided an update on the same.

minutes_note:
CITY ATTORNEY TOLCES read the Quasi-Judicial statement, explained the procedure and asked the City Commission if there were any disclosures regarding this Item.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ said only the City Manager during her Agenda Review.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE said only the City Manager.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO believed he spoke to everybody.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO believed it was only the City Manager.
MAYOR ARSERIO spoke to the City Manager, with the operator and their attorney, Matt Scott and staff.
CITY ATTORNEY TOLCES directed the City Commission individually and as a collective with further instructions. He received a request from Development Services Director, Taschereau, asking whether staff could go first and confirmed that he could not see any objection from that request. He advised on the swearing-in procedure if anyone was going to speak on this Item.
DEVELOPMENT SERVICES (DS), SENIOR PLANNER, ANDREW PINNEY, went through a quick PowerPoint presentation to the Special Exception hearing for a proposed Dunkin'. He provided detail on the subject property and discussed its history which used to be the BankAtlantic location and also a donut restaurant, both which had drive-throughs and in 2003, the City Commission passed a Resolution to redevelop the site. He advised that Clutch Coffee submitted an application in 2021 but after approval, did not move forward on the site. He continued to go through the site plan and logistics of this Item and explained the City Commission’s role in determining the outcome. He also provided the 10 conditions for Special Exception General Standards of Review which detailed staff findings through the Development Review Committee (DRC) process. He said that the DRC recommended a Conditional Approval on February 24th and that the Planning and Zoning (P&Z) Board recommended a conditional approval on April 7th. He explained that at the April meeting, the applicant in review of the P&Z Board indicated that during peak periods, they would have employees outside in the drive-thru area with electronic devices taking orders to help manage the traffic and as they represented that at the hearing, it would become a condition of an approval.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO thanked DS Senior Planner, Pinney and questioned the vote from the P&Z Board. He agreed with the findings and did not see a problem and hoped that this Item passed. He suggested that during their opening week or month, they should give free donuts to the Police and Fire employees.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ questioned whether the building was going to remain exactly how it was with the exception of the Dunkin’ logo. She indicated that the site was a drive-through bank and was not keen on the design. She did not envisage Dunkin’ to look that way and voiced her concerns on the operational procedures.
DS SENIOR PLANNER, PINNEY responded to Commissioner Schwartz’s query and discussed one of the elevations that he attached to his PowerPoint presentation.
Discussion ensued on the design, the code and the threshold.
MAYOR ARSERIO said that the property had been vacant for a while and highlighted previous applicants. He said that anything would be better than how it currently looked and said that having spoken to a representative, he was informed that they had won Dunkin’ Operator of the Year nationwide. He expressed that they take pride in what they did and said that it would be a good fit for Margate.
Discussion ensued.
GREENSPOON MARDER (GM), PARTNER, ELIZABETH SOMERSTEIN, 200 E. BROWARD BLVD. represented the applicant and provided a PowerPoint presentation. She explained that it was a very challenging site which was under half an acre and she also discussed the issue that faced Clutch Coffee. She highlighted the improvements that they intended to make on the current site which included enhancing the landscaping and revitalizing the existing building.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ did not recall the City asking Clutch Coffee to spend an enormous amount of money to improve the site.
Discussion ensued on improvements to the site
GM, PARTNER, SOMERSTEIN, continued with her presentation and discussed the on site elevations. She confirmed that the applicant had met all the criteria and was awaiting the City Commission’s discretion to determine compliance.
Discussion ensued.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO envisaged that the back-up line would only be in the morning and did not anticipate it being that long for the rest of the day.
GM, PARTNER, SOMERSTEIN met code’s requirements as they completed a queuing analysis which actually indicated that at a 95% rate, they would only need stacking for two cars.
Discussion ensued.
MAYOR ARSERIO opened the hearing to members of the public who had been sworn in.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ referenced that check marks were not in the presentation that the City Commission received.
MARGATE RESIDENT, TRACY VAN WINKLE, addressed her issues pertaining to this Item.
MAYOR ARSERIO responded to Ms. Winkle’s comments.
MR. ZUCCHINI explained that the P&Z board had unanimously approved it. He also discussed a queue line analysis.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO responded to Ms. Winkle’s comments.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO discussed the rise of drive-through establishments and referenced Cali Coffee. He did not have a problem with this Item and said that he did not want to see empty buildings in Margate.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE felt sorry for Clutch Coffee when they pulled out as she was disappointed that the City made it extremely difficult for them. She welcomed Dunkin’ and had no problem with them making use of that property and hoped that it could spark the shopping center to make improvements.
MR. KRALJIC did not necessarily oppose the project but highlighted his areas of concern.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ asked for the typical hours for Dunkin’ and referenced Mr. Kraljic’s comment about deliveries.
GM, PARTNER, SOMERSTEIN, provided the operational hours for Dunkin’ and said that they have a dedicated loading zone and they had already completed a truck analysis.
CITY ATTORNEY TOLCES provided further instructions on the City Commission’s decision making.

minutes_note:
MAYOR, ANTONIO V. ARSERIO, welcomed former City Manager May back to Margate.
INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR BROWARD SOLID WASTE AUTHORITY (BSWA), SAM A. MAY, introduced some of his peers who were present from respective organizations within Broward County (BC).
A BSWA REPRESENTATIVE spoke on this matter and thanked Vice Mayor Caggiano for doing a fantastic job on the Executive Committee who he said had been instrumental in assisting with writing the master plan that the 28 cities of BC had put together. He said the changes would include a very big effort to determine where the garbage would go and how it was disposed of in the most egonomical, cost effective and environmental correct way and referenced running out of landfill space. He highlighted that their recycling rate was cut in half which had decreased from approximately 60% to 30% and their landfill rate doubled which was not a good place to be. He said that a presentation will be made but the City Commission would be voting on the lynchpin which had to be passed by August 14th.
INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR BSWA, MAY, thanked the Department of Environmental and Engineering Services (DEES) Solid Waste and Sustainability Coordinator, Yapp, who was also on the Technical Advisory Committee (TAC) and said that she had been very instrumental in assisting them. He provided a brief synopsis of his experience and expertise of working in BC. He conducted a PowerPoint presentation and highlighted the cities that have confirmed their participation in this program. He said that currently, there was a fragmented system where everybody was there but had the global agreement that BC put together and indicated that many were paying a lot more who were not participants. He explained why the change was necessary and informed that the South Waste Authority (SWA) would utilize the existing infrastructure that was already available in BC. He said that almost all of the people (entities) who were part of this infrastructure such as the processing facilities and the disposal sites were all in favor of this. He indicated that they would be able to improve their infrastructure and get a return on their investments. He read through the funding flow and explained that it would cost the average home $3 per year.
MAYOR ARSERIO referenced the proposed ballot amendment for the elimination of property taxes and that they were allegedly putting other restrictions on cities to increase their fees or to offset costs somewhere else. He questioned that if the voters passed it, would it prevent them from adding a non-ad valorem assessment?
INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR BSWA, MAY, informed that some cities have their solid waste assessment which was a bill that was part of non-ad valorem and he did not believe it would change.
CITY ATTORNEY, DAVID N. TOLCES, advised that the legislation pertaining to the taxes was passed yesterday which would be on the ballot in November and explained that they were still reviewing and analyzing it and said that it was focused on ad valorem taxation which was based upon an assessed value.
INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR BSWA, MAY, continued with the PowerPoint presentation and briefly discussed the funding mechanisms and said that the rates listed on the Maximum Service Charges for Materials Processing were part of the global agreement, which expired in 2028 and could possibly be extended and would increase yearly due to the Consumer Price Index (CPI).
MAYOR ARSERIO referenced the single stream recycling and said it was one of the big contributors to contamination. He questioned how they would increase the recycling percentages and referenced an incinerator.
INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR BSWA, MAY said that Fomento de Construcciones y Contratas Environmental Services’ (FCC) proposal was to add an additional boiler if the solid waste authority moved forward.
Discussion ensued.
INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR BSWA, MAY explained that the City had already signed the ILA and that the facilities amendment would need to be signed to move forward and he also explained the next steps.
COMMISSIONER, ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ, indicated that education would probably not be so difficult pertaining to a single stream system.
VICE PRESIDENT (VP) AND PROJECT DIRECTOR OF STEARNS, CONRAD & SCHMIDT, (SCS) ENGINEERS, DANIEL E. DIETCH, compared single stream versus dual stream recycling.
MAYOR ARSERIO announced that Coconut Creek’s (CC) City Commissioner, Rydell was available on Zoom.
COMMISSIONER, TOMMY RUZZANO, welcomed CC’s City Commissioner Rydell and former City Manager May. He questioned the cut-off date and whether there were any cities that were opposed to this agreement. He thanked them for attending this meeting.
VP OF SCS ENGINEERS, DIETCH, confirmed that 15 August was the cut-off date and he discussed the interlocal agreement.
INTERIM EXECUTIVE DIRECTOR FOR BSWA, MAY, said that some cities were opposed due to the opt-out which they were going to.
Discussion ensued.

minutes_note:
CITY MANAGER CURTIS, explained that this Item was the change order pertaining to residents’ feedback and that they did not want to eliminate the basketball court. He said that they petitioned the City Commission to have Margate look into obtaining pricing to redesign and cost of construction for completing that project with the three components of basketball, pickleball and tennis at that court.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO explained that he agreed with a resident that he did not want the basketball courts removed and indicated that the proposed increase price of $530,000 for the redesign was too high. He questioned whether the high increase also factored in whether the City was redesigning the property for the stormwater. He said that he would not mind seeing a 20 x 20 concrete slab with a basketball hoop. He believed that this park was being funded by every taxpayer so that everyone could visit yet some only wanted tennis courts. He realized that pickleball was more popular these days but it would encourage more people than those playing basketball.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS responded to Commissioner Ruzzano and said that it was not just that as they could not leave the basketball court that way due to its current state. He explained the original design plan and how the cost had affected the new design including the improvision of stormwater retention. He explained that after receiving feedback, they were trying to appease the desire of many users of the park and they have received a price from their contractor to do that.
Discussion ensued on the stormwater and the construction projects.
MAYOR ARSERIO indicated that the neighborhood had a history of being divided and referenced speed bumps. He said that although he was in favor of keeping the basketball court, he would take Commissioner Ruzzano’s expertise that the $500,000 was too expensive.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ said that they built the dog park for approximately $500,000. She informed the City Manager that it was a City park and recommended a sign being erected as it was being treated as a community park. She agreed with Commissioner Ruzzano on installing a 20 x 20 basketball court but could not comprehend it costing the same as the dog park.
Discussion ensued.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS advised that if this Item did not pass or get motioned, they would move forward with the contract that the City Commission approved which was an upgrade to the playground and replacing the basketball court with a tennis court. He said that if the City Commission preferred to retain the basketball court as it would probably be a much easier thing to do and indicated that the basketball hoops would need to be upgraded but would be substantially less.
Discussion ensued on retaining and renovating the basketball court.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS questioned that if it did not pass, he would welcome direction from the City Commission if they wanted them to revisit refurbishing the basketball court and eliminating the tennis court.
Discussion ensued.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO was informed that on the basketball court, epoxy could be applied to enhance the surface.
Discussion ensued including on how it would be paid for.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE recommended a workshop to include the residents’ feedback due to the back and forth on the proposals.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS advised that the City was well past due on using the bond funds, believed that they had enough information and that they had already received feedback via a community survey and through social media and that the costs was the most expensive. He suggested that they could leave the original design, finish that project and revisit installing a pad independently for a basketball court at a later date. He recommended not to move forward with this change order, complete the project and they could evaluate expanding it in the future and adding in a basketball or pickleball courts as trends change.
Discussion ensued including the contingency money be moved out for a concrete slab.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS stated there was no motion, no second and that this change order fails. His direction is to move forward with the existing design, as is, with the tennis and pickleball courts and identifying what the contingency was, to find a way to install a pad for basketball and report back.

minutes_note:
DISTRICT 96 – FLORIDA STATE REPRESENTATIVE (FSR) CHRISTINE HUNSCHOFSKY said that both her and Senator Polsky both represented Margate amongst other cities in Northwest Broward and that they were going to give a brief legislative update and referenced redistricting and congressional seats. She discussed some of the tough bills that they had this last session which included Senate Bill (SB) 1134: Official Actions of Local Governments which prevented local governments from taking any action on matters such as diversity, equity and inclusion efforts.
STATE SENATOR TINA POLSKY elaborated on SB 1134 and referenced Oktoberfest as an example and discussed SB 1217: Prohibited Governmental Policies Regulating Greenhouse Gas Emissions and also referenced net zero emissions. She brought attention to the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility Act (SAVE America Act) and highlighted the issues it could cause.
DISTRICT 96 – FSR HUNSCHOFSKY advised that the SB 382 e-bike safety bill was vetoed by the Florida State Governor. She said that the SB 1434 was the Infill Redevelopment Act which was not great and explained it allowed certain remediated contaminated properties of brownfields to be redeveloped for housing. She felt positive of the Florida HB 1085 (Local Government Cyber Security) which was recently signed into law and SB 984 Firefighter Cancer Benefits. She read an extract of a statement from the Florida Professional Firefighters pertaining to the PTA 3.
SENATOR POLSKY gave an update on the Property Tax Amendment 3 (PTA) which required 60% for it to pass and urged the public to do their own research and listen to their elected officials. She hoped that they would be able to explain to them how much less revenue they would receive for services that were essential such as police, fire, parks and environmental concerns, drainage roads and senior centers.
DISTRICT 96 – FSR HUNSCHOFSKY explained that it was very important for voters to do their homework and referenced having a town hall recently where she illustrated her Truth in Millage (TRIM).
SENATOR POLSKY informed that after eight years, she was not running for re-election and thanked the City for their support and said she had another six months before she departed. She highlighted that FSR Hunschofsky had been reelected without opposition and would continue to represent Margate. She announced that State Florida Governor DeSantis finally signed the budget which was $117,630,000 and conducted a check presentation of $350,000 to Margate which was for their stormwater infrastructure system.
MAYOR, ANTONIO V. ARSERIO, referenced the PTA 3 and thanked the elected officials for discussing renters. He encouraged the public to do their homework, thanked FSR Hunschofsky and referenced SB 1434 was the Infill Redevelopment Act which targeted golf courses.
VICE MAYOR, ANTHONY N. CAGGIANO, concurred with Mayor Arserio’s comments on FSR Hunschofsky and said that she had always been fighting for Margate.
COMMISSIONER, TOMMY RUZZANO, thanked the two elected officials. He questioned whether the PTA 3 would eventually phase out taxes.
CITY ATTORNEY, DAVID N. TOLCES, advised Commissioner Ruzzano that the PTA 3 did not provide for the complete phase out of property taxes as it was 150 then 250.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO said that there was a difference of opinion between the Republicans and the Democrats in Tallahassee and Broward County (BC) on PTA 3 and referenced a broken tax system and Broward County Property Appraiser. He expressed it was a tough decision.
COMMISSIONER, JOANNE SIMONE, thanked and praised the elected officials for their hard efforts and wished Senator Polsky the best in her endeavors.
COMMISSIONER ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ, thanked the FRSs and warned the public to be careful voting against their own self-interest. She said that they should have looked at property insurance instead.
VICE MAYOR, CAGGIANO said if the PTA 3 passed, there would not be money from BC for mosquito spraying as it was not considered a core service and indicated that it could become inhabitable within a quick succession of time.
title: LEGISLATIVE UPDATE BY STATE REPRESENTATIVE CHRISTINE HUNSCHOFSKY, DISTRICT 95 AND STATE SENATOR TINA POLSKY, DISTRICT 30

COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ, highlighted Margate’s 4th of July Parade & Fireworks event. She questioned the City Manager about the upkeep of the Carolina Golf Course and referenced mowing the grass.
CITY MANAGER, CALE CURTIS, believed that the owner of the Carolina Golf Course had a repeat order and confirmed that if they did not pay, the property could be liened.
Discussion ensued on the Carolina Golf Course.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE sent her condolences and support to the people of Venezuela due to the recent devastation and requested the public to keep them in their thoughts and prayers. She also sent her deepest condolences to the family of former MPD Officer, Lonnie Donahue. She congratulated MPD for their reaccreditation from the CFA. She informed City Manager Curtis that the manhole covers on Margate Boulevard were a little bit low. She highlighted the weather forecast for the 4th of July Parade and forewarned of the dangers and debris caused from lighting fireworks at home. She read a statement discussing her concerns that Mr. Wallach was still looking and posting that he was opening up a store in Margate despite not having any city, state or federal license to display exotic animals. She also provided education on kangaroo facts and behaviors. She asked the City Commission to give CONSENSUS for the City Manager and staff to impose a moratorium on issuing any license or permit for any pet related stores or any facility with live animals excluding a dog or cat rescue organization for one year.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO questioned Commissioner Simone if she put an exemption in place to house animals when pet owners were away.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE confirmed that she would.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO, explained that there was no way that he could support it. He thought it was personal and said that they should not go after somebody due to their past history and did not believe that the City should put in a moratorium.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO thanked Commissioner Simone for her views.
Discussion ensued.
MAYOR ARSERIO said that he did not support animal cruelty but indicated that Commissioner Simone was looking at punishing a whole industry as she was not in agreement with one of them.
Discussion ensued on whether Mr. Wallach could open a pet store in Margate.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ, explained that she did not have a problem with imposing a moratorium right now and to review the rules.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO requested City Manager Curtis or City Attorney to look into this and see if Margate could come up with some rules.
MAYOR ARSERIO indicated that he was not for a blanket rule but if there were particular things they could tweak, he would listen.
CITY ATTORNEY, DAVID N. TOLCES, said that if there was CONSENSUS to direct the City Manager and City Attorney to research the issue to see if any kind of Ordinance that would enact some type of moratorium, they could do that and revert to the City Commission. He was aware that Orange County was discussing this issue and referenced Sloth World.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS, questioned if the direction to come back with an Ordinance for a moratorium on pet stores on issuing any licenses and permits to pet stores or was the direction to come back with an Ordinance that implements restrictions on the types of animals that can be placed in a pet store.
Discussion ensued.
CITY ATTORNEY TOLCES said that they would look to see what they could do to bring it back for July 8th but if not, they would inform the City Commission accordingly.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO congratulated FSR Hunschofsky who ran unopposed. He referenced a conversation by a public speaker pertaining to a lobbyist and said that there was a project going on at the golf course and that he was totally against developing it. He referenced the tow truck companies and understood that the City would be losing money no matter what they did with the contract and informed that the rates were set by BC which could not be tweaked. He wished America a happy 250th birthday and highlighted Margate’s 4th of July Parade and also wished his son a happy 18th birthday.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO discussed hurricane preparedness. He highlighted the City’s 4th of July Parade and Fireworks event. He also discussed the Venezuela devastation.
MAYOR ARSERIO was excited for the weekend to celebrate America’s 250th birthday and indicated that Margate’s 4th of July Parade was always well attended and that they did not suspend their event during the pandemic. He requested people not to set off fireworks at midnight and to be responsible for the clean-up that followed. He congratulated MPD for getting reaccredited. He said that the road was coming together in time for the Parade. He commented on some of the plants on the roundabout and questioned whether they were supposed to be swapped out. He also questioned whether there was a date for the sand bag distribution and spoke of the importance to be proactive and plan this in advance.
.

minutes_note:
CITY MANAGER CURTIS, explained that they received an unsolicited proposal for the operation of a soccer club in Margate and that it would be appropriate for this board to provide direction to staff. He advised that per state statute, if the City Commission wanted to entertain proposals for a service such this, it would have to go through a competitive solicitation.
Discussion ensued on the procedural requirements.
MAYOR ARSERIO invited Mr. Scott to conduct his presentation.
GREENSPOON MARDER (GM), PARTNER, MATTHEW H. SCOTT, 200 E. BROWARD BLVD. represented Fort Lauderdale Football Club LLC and explained that under state statute, they submitted an unsolicited proposal. He advised that this Item was not to seek approval but it was simply for them to present this unsolicited proposal. He introduced his client, Tom Smith.
FORT LAUDERDALE UNITED (FLU) FOOTBALL CLUB, CHAIR, TOMMY SMITH repeated Mr. Scott’s comments that they were here to submit a proposal and the way of a partnership. He said that they were a division one women’s professional team and the men’s professional team would be effective from 2027. He presented a PowerPoint presentation and said that they had approximately 3,000 youth kids across different sports. He continued to discuss their history and current location. He said as part of the proposal, it would guarantee the City $100,000 per year for the upkeep of fields and also to take over the maintenance and the facilities at Oriole Park. He said that the basis of the program was to make it a Margate centric program and that partnering with the Gainbridge United Soccer League (USL) was to install a mini pitch at one of the City’s designated parks which had a value of approximately $500,000. He summed it up by saying that they wanted to partner with Margate and referenced revenue share for anything they collect.
GM, PARTNER, SCOTT said that they were not proposing to take over recreational soccer. He explained that they would work with their Parks and Recreation Director to arrange scheduling so it would not impact any of the recreational sports. He understood that the City was unable to get flag football off the ground. He advised that they had specific experience and expertise in which they could help get this league off the ground and with their resources, they could also help take their travel team to the next level. He indicated that during the non-season, they could also provide free clinics for the community at their parks.
MAYOR ARSERIO questioned that in addition to the revenue share and $100,000 for annual leave for field improvements, if that was in addition to the full rental and that they were not asking for a discount on the field rentals. He also understood that there would be scholarship opportunities. He questioned whether their fees be similar, cheaper or more achievable than what they currently have.
FLU CHAIR, SMITH confirmed that they were not asking for a discount on field rentals and indicated that there would be scholarship. He aimed to make the fees as affordable as possible.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE understood that the purpose tonight was not to pick anybody but to ask the City if they wanted to open it up to other bids and it appeared that this league was making a pitch with this presentation. She was confused as to why this proposal was being allowed to be pitched if they were only asking if the City wanted to go out to other organizations to solicit them as well. She did not think it was appropriate to pitch this tonight if that was not the intent of what they were trying to do. She read all of the proposals and had several questions but said that if that was not the intent, she did not want to go into her list of concerns.
CITY ATTORNEY TOLCES explained that under the Statute, there was an obligation that if the City received an unsolicited proposal for the governing body (City Commission) to decide whether or not they wanted to go out and solicit other proposals, they could only go about this at a public meeting and have it on the Agenda. He advised that there were many steps to discuss before negotiating an agreement.
Discussion ensued on exploring options.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE expressed her concerns and raised a number of questions on this proposal.
Discussion ensued.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS advised Commissioner Simone that she was asking and pointing out excellent questions in terms of the agreement and that they were almost identical to what they had already identified and that if they got an opportunity to negotiate a comprehensive agreement, those were the areas that they would focus on.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE thought that this Item had come up too short, too fast and not enough time to really get into it. She had not heard of any problems or that they were interested in any of this nor had she heard from the P & R Director Jones.
MAYOR ARSERIO explained the process to Commissioner Simone.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ analyzed that it was a pitch but to make them aware that certain things could be better and realized that the City did not run the travel soccer and that Margate had no oversight. She said that she did not have a problem looking at some of those things.
Discussion ensued.
GM, PARTNER, SCOTT said that if they were to move forward, the travel soccer would not start until Spring. He said that the idea would be to introduce themselves to the community by doing free clinics in the fall.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO questioned whether they would allow the public to speak on this Item. He indicated that he was confused about this Item and suggested a workshop.
MAYOR ARSERIO explained that he would allow the public to speak.
Discussion ensued including travel sports and entering into an agreement.
MR. ZUCCHINI said that any type of sports activity that the City could help support and organize was well worth it and he was in support of this Item. He suggested that if there was any revenue generated, it should be used to create an athletic scholarship program.
DARRYL D. MAURO, 2100 N.W. 62ND AVENUE, explained that they already provide a service for the City and said that certain things are not permissible through Parks and Recreation and that they have to submit a proposal for renting the fields. He discussed some of the comments that were made during the presentation.
MAYOR ARSERIO suggested Mr. Mauro to submit a proposal.
Discussion ensued.
MARGATE RESIDENT, MARLON POLO said that he had been the Coaching Director in Margate for 20 years and referenced that Margate United FC had been operating for 47 years. He said that it was a family group and he did not believe it was for a business.
MARGATE RESIDENT, SEAN FLETCHER, discussed his role as a coach and made comment on this proposal. He advised that the City should make this a community decision and requested Margate to research.
MAYOR ARSERIO responded to Mr. Fletcher’s comments and encouraged people to submit proposals for them to pick the best one.
PRESIDENT OF MARGATE UNITED FC, MICHAEL POLO, discussed how he went through the ranks and agreed with Mayor Arserio to put this out for a bid.
MS. BERACHA discussed how this Item was presented and referenced unfairness.
ANDREW WATSON, spoke about Margate Kids and paid tribute to Michael Polo.
MAYOR ARSERIO continued to speak on this Item, he appreciated all of the volunteer work of what the coaches did and explained that they wanted a competitive process.
PARKS AND RECREATION (P&R) DIRECTOR, MICHAEL A. JONES, provided a historical insight on this Item and explained that there was no existing contract as there was never a need for one as it was a volunteer ran organization. He said that Margate had always been a grass roots program. He said that the City found some bad behavior amongst parents in some of their sports and this was when they decided to run a City rec program. He believed that travel sports should not be a City service hence why they did not put it out for a bid to hire anyone and let the private sector run it. He said that the options were that they either run it inhouse, they partner with another organization which would help lower some of the costs as it was pretty large for the average family and that way, it was a partnership and it was not anything other than renting fields which would be all about the kids, player development and coach development. He suggested that they should host a workshop with the public, City Commission and any proposals but would need to know what the City Commission wanted and to receive direction from the City Manager what their end goal was to enable him to provide that recommendation. He said that having a partnership with sponsors was not a bad thing as ultimately, it lowered the cost to the player and their family.
