CITY MANAGER, CALE CURTIS, announced that it was Margate’s first City Commission Budget Workshop for Fiscal Year 2027. He thanked the Finance Department team and the Department Heads for their efforts and explained that it was a long process that started last January.
BUDGET MANAGER (BM), DECIA A. SMITH-BURKE, welcomed everyone to the FY 2027 Proposed Budget Workshop. She said that although they conducted the presentation every year at relatively the same time with the same information, this year, they were looking at it from a different perspective. She highlighted that they were awarded the FY2026 Distinguished Budget Presentation Award for the ninth time and that the City was also awarded a special recognition for strategic goals and priorities. She advised that the proposed City millage rate for Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 was 7.5185 which included both operating and debt service millage rate. She confirmed that the operating millage rate was proposed to remain at 7.1171. She discussed the decade of Tax Revenue and said that $37,792,820, was proposed based on the June 2026 values which would be updated for July. She said that although the City was budgeting approximately $1,800,000 in additional ad valorem revenue, the change in property values also result in an increase in the payment to the Community Redevelopment Agency (CRA) for FY2027 and it was over $467,000 which meant that the net change for the General Fund budget property tax revenue was $1,300,000. She also informed that although the values increased this year, the overall property tax values in Margate were much lower than the average in Broward County (BC) and that 7% of Margate residents paid no ad valorem revenue taxes which resulted in approximately 30% paying less than $500 for a year’s worth of services. She continued to go through the PowerPoint presentation by highlighting that Margate had one of the most reasonable tax burdens when averaging Homesteaded Single-Family compared to other cities in BC. She also highlighted that Margate was in the third lowest in dollar amount of city tax when explaining the Operating Revenue Per Capita Comparison. She informed that Margate revenue per capita was $645 which was the sixth lowest cost city to live in for the value that was provided.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS pertained to the last two PowerPoint slides and said that this was something to be proud of as Margate was one of the lowest which was a full service city. He elaborated by saying that arguably, Margate delivered service equal to any one of the municipalities listed and were doing it at a much lower tax burden to their residents in comparison to other cities.
BM, SMITH-BURKE, continued with her PowerPoint presentation. She summarized the FY 2027 Proposed Budget and Capital Improvement Program. She repeated that they were proposing for the millage rate to decrease based on their debt service reducing from 7.5378 in FY2026 to 7.5185. She sought CONSENSUS on the millage rate ceiling for FY2027 which meant that the rate set today could not be exceeded.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS informed that they added new slides to the PowerPoint presentation to incorporate an outlook on what the tax reform may look like for the City should it pass in November 2026. He said that if the public vote in the affirmative of the ballot question in the next election, it would increase the Homestead exemption for residential Homesteaded properties from $50,000 to $150,000 which would be effective January 2027. He said that the Homestead exemption of $150,000 would then be applied to the November 2027 tax bills where the first impact would be in FY2028. He explained that in January 2028, the second phase of that Homestead exemption would apply and the Homestead exemption would be $250,000 which would be effective in November 2028 tax bill which would be FY2029 impact for the City. He indicated that in FY2028, the City would be looking at approximately $8,000,000 reduction in ad valorem revenue and in FY2029, $12,100,000 reduction in revenue and the figures were based off of assessed values from this current year’s assessment. He continued to discuss components to how the Proposed Tax Bill and that non-residential valuations would be capped. He said that the legislator passed this at their July session, the City took some immediate action such as implementing a hiring and travel freeze and gone through a 10% internal General Fund budget reduction exercise and how they could raise revenue such as school zone speed cameras. He also highlighted that there was some new revenue on the horizon with new development that was going on in the City.
MAYOR, ANTONIO V. ARSERIO, believed that the City was taking the right approach and he did envisage that there would be some type of tax reform occurring but until they find out what takes place, he thought that they were responsible and they do have certain freezes in place. He highlighted that the City’s total millage rate had decreased over the last two years.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS explained that the objective of this Workshop was to set the tentative maximum millage rate but it was also an opportunity for the City Commission to raise any questions if they were seeking clarification so that they can return with a proposed formal budget to them in September.
MAYOR ARSERIO referenced median enhancements which he indicated were not in the budget and sought consideration from the City Commission to funding at least $250,000 which would continue to beautify their City.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER, ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ, questioned where the funds would come from.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS explained that the City was fortunate to have a very good landscape supervisor in Parks and Recreation who was doing many of the design and management of the work inhouse and was also able to stretch those funds pretty significantly. He said that the monies would come from an unsigned fund balance.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER, JOANNE SIMONE, said that whilst she thought beautification was important, she would not be in favor of spending $250,000 to do that and suggested looking for other grants to make up the costs.
Discussion ensued.
VICE MAYOR, ANTHONY N. CAGGIANO, gave Mayor Arserio’s his second “yes” as he agreed with his $250,000 median enhancement proposal.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ agreed as long as it was not all palm trees and commented on looking beyond Rock Island Road.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO said it looked horrible down south and his preference would be to see contour in the medians and color.
Discussion ensued including medians and the costs to maintain the same.
VICE MAYOR CAGGIANO appreciated the City for running a tight budget.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO was in disagreement about the budgeted Item for the City Chambers improvements.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS advised that the City Chambers Item had been budgeted and rebudgeted over the last few years. He requested retaining money in that budget for any audio visual upgrades.
MAYOR ARSERIO said that although the City Chambers could do with a face lift, he questioned whether tax payers needed to pay for that right now. He indicated that he was content in holding off from doing any type of major renovations but recommended retaining some funds for any essential items.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS suggested reducing Mayor Arserio's median enhancement suggestion to $150,000. He advised that vehicles were listed in Operating Expenses under rentals and leases and referenced that there were a few specialty type vehicles that were more beneficial to purchase instead of leasing.
Discussion ensued on the vehicle programing.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO wanted to see the canals cleaned. He referenced the possible revenue of the Local Business Tax Receipt (LBTR) and voiced his concerns that if they were going to lose money from the residents, then they may go after the businesses which he was not a big fan of. He also referenced the new revenue streams and said that school zone speed cameras was originally presented as a safety feature for the residents but now it was a money grab which he had always alluded to. He suggested that the Developer’s Agreement should be reviewed again as it was something that would make or break the City. He thought it was a good budget.
Discussion ensued on the Marquesa and Forest Apartments projects and how much revenue it would generate and also reviewing the liquor licenses.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ referenced curb appeal and suggested that the rug in the City Chambers should be changed. She suggested that the fees for Calypso Cove be increased as it was only being utilized by 33% of their residents. She referenced 85% and discussed performance levels and requested that the department heads should meet the City’s goals and objectives. She thanked the City for the budget and forewarned on the Florida Amendment 3.
Discussion ensued on rugs and the acoustics of the City Chambers.
CITY MANAGER CURTIS looked for an affirmative on setting the tentative maximum millage rate at 7.1171 which was the same rate as the prior year.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER SIMONE thanked the departments for putting together this Budget and said that they did a fantastic job. She agreed with some of the comments made by her peers and referenced the speed cameras which she was never in favor of. She hoped that future City Commissioners will look at some of the feel good things that were in the budget and not approve them in light of Florida Amendment 3.
MAYOR ARSERIO believed that the City Manager received direction.
title: FY 2026-2027 BUDGET WORKSHOP

title: DISCUSSION AND POSSIBLE ACTION

minutes_note:
CITY MANAGER, CALE CURTIS, explained that the City received an unsolicited proposal from Fort Lauderdale United (FLU) to operate a competitive football/travel soccer program which was presented at a recent City Commission meeting where they sought the board’s direction. He informed that there were statutory requirements on how the City handled public/private partnerships and unsolicited proposals He informed that they held a very productive town hall and that it was brought back to this City Commission meeting for further discussion and that the City had some options on how they proceed from here. He said that the two high priorities they received so far was to have an affordable competitive program in the City for the Margate community. He inquired that if it was the City Commission’s desire to find a provider that could do that, they had a couple of options of finding a partner. He said that the three options were:
1) To move forward with the unsolicited public/private partnership proposal that was received and follow the state’s statutes;
2) Reject the proposal they received and devise their own Request for Proposal (RFP); or
3) Reject the bid and continue operating the way they were.
MAYOR, ANTONIO V. ARSERIO, indicated that this unsolicited bid had opened his eyes to how sports were operated and said it was interesting that the City had no current agreement. He informed that Margate had a wonderful group of people such as dedicated coaches, volunteers and parents which were involved and players and student athletes which were important to their community and that he wanted to recognize those efforts. He said on paper from a City perspective, they do not have a soccer program and explained that he wanted it to be more than a group renting their fields. He recommended as a City, they should have their own program or some type of partnership where a contractual agreement was in place with terms and conditions. He advised that he was in favor of the first two options. He did not attend the town hall meetings to avoid any influence.
COMMISSIONER, TOMMY RUZZANO, thanked the public for attending this City Commission meeting and said that he had been involved in baseball coaching for over 20 years. He advised that Margate Recreational Soccer was not going anywhere. He highlighted a previous issue with a travel group running the baseball league which conflicted upon the availability on the City's facilities. He attended a meeting and understood the sentiments of the public wanting something to the next level which he did not have a problem with and said that the majority were in favor of option two pertaining to an RFP. He made a few suggestions of how they could minimize the length of discussing this Item. He thanked Sean for getting involved with this Item which resulted in a strong attendance for this meeting.
MAYOR ARSERIO said that he listened to the Town Hall meeting and read online comments and thanked Mr. Fletcher for being very thoughtful and fair and referenced, affordability, protecting rec but also giving students a pathway into travel and professional soccer or collegiate opportunities. He explained that he did not have a problem with going out to bid which the City would have to review which could also be rejected.
.
COMMISSIONER, ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ, said that she attended the meeting and thought there was a misunderstanding for option 1 and explained there was no need for an RFP as it would allow the City to spend a fortune. She was fine with option 1 and did not see a need for an RFP.
Discussion ensued.
VICE MAYOR, ANTHONY N. CAGGIANO, agreed 100% with Commissioner Schwartz's comments.
COMMISSIONER RUZZANO, predicted that it was going to be option one which he did not agree with but would consider option two but indicated that the decision should come down to what the residents want. He suggested making a partnership with this group and that if the soccer fields were not used by the recreational teams, Margate travel would receive next priority and suggested to conduct it in the same way as the policy that the City wrote approximately 10 years ago which was approved by a previous City Commission.
Discussion ensued.
VICE MAYOR, CAGGIANO, said that at no point are they forced to accept any bid and that they can say “no” to anybody. He explained that there was an opportunity to learn and see what was best for the residents.
CITY ATTORNEY, DAVID N. TOLCES, provided instruction for Public Comments pertaining to this Item.
MARGATE RESIDENT, MINDY W. LEE, stated that an owner donated to Mayor Arserio’s campaign earlier this year.
MAYOR ARSERIO denied the allegations.
Discussion ensued.
MARGATE RESIDENT, SEAN A. FLETCHER, acknowledged the Parks and Recreation Department and referenced conversing with their Director, Mr. Jones. He urged the City Commission to choose option two.
MARGATE UNITED FOOTBALL CLUB (MUFC), DIRECTOR OF COACHING, MICHAEL POLO, said that they had been there for a long time, they had the infrastructure and the staff and was awaiting the City’s confirmation and green light to build a bridge program. He questioned why they would bring an external program with no ties to the City.
A question and answer session ensued between Mr. Polo and Commissioner Schwartz.
COMMISSIONER SCHWARTZ, referenced revenue and said that Mr. Polo may be grassroots but he was attached to organizations which were attached to others that were way passed that.
Discussion ensued on MUFC.
MARK DARLING, 2100 NE 4TH AVENUE, worked for the bridge company to MUFC. He said that when he first came to Margate, they previously met with P&R to make some type of agreement and to be more involved with the City.
A question and answer session ensued between Mr. Darling and Commissioner Schwartz.
MARIANA URIBE, 6124 NW 22ND STREET, said at the end of the day, it was always about money and explained that he wanted to stay in Margate.
JASON MARAJ, 6999 CHARLESTON COURT, lived at the same address for 26 years and had coached at Margate United FC with the Polos for approximately eight years and due to the issues in the City, he was now with Athletic Club Florida (ACF). He urged the City to do personal research and referenced intangibles.
MIRAMAR RESIDENT drove approximately four times per week to train at ACF. She explained that a group of parents decided to do a petition for the City to do a transparent process in this selection of who was running the public/private partnership.
LIONEL BROWN explained that up until 2004, he was part of Margate’s first travel team and said that they have the ability to make a partnership.
A question and answer session ensued between Mr. Brown and Commissioner Schwartz.
CORAL SPRINGS RESIDENT, CARLOS M. GUTIERREZ, explained that ACF was a club that came before anybody else to bring an opportunity for Margate to have the exposure that they did not have before. He said that they were putting money in front of the kids which did not happen overseas.
DARRYL MAURO, 2100 NW 62ND AVENUE, was a 50 year resident and created East Florida United in 1988. He referenced that he conversed with an AFC representative and that they wanted to partnership with everyone which he indicated could be achieved.
MARGATE RESIDENT, TRACY VAN WINKLE, suggested that the City work on obtaining a contract to help the Margate residents and kids instead of selling them out. She said that it did not work with baseball which Margate had to take back.
MAYOR ARSERIO responded to Ms. Van Winkle’s comment.
Discussion ensued.
MARGATE RESIDENT, DONNA L. FELLOWS, quoted Mayor Arserio saying that if the residents want to be heard, they should attend the meetings. She alluded that the City Commission’s audience was Margate’s future and that the City should not sell them out.
MAYOR ARSERIO responded to Ms. Fellows’ comment.
Discussion ensued.
MARGATE RESIDENT, JONATHAN KRALJIC, read a statement saying that decisions from the dais needed to be made based on the people’s wants and demands.
MARGATE RESIDENT, THERESA BOOKER, expressed that "Margate should be for Margate" and agreed with Commissioner Ruzzano's comment that they should allow soccer players to assist in developing the City's program.
COMMISSIONER, JOANNE SIMONE, suggested that Mr. Mauro and Mr. Fletcher should liaise with P&R Director Jones and City Manager Curtis to work out an agreement. She recommended that MUFC and ACF should all come together for the benefit of the children.

DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC AFFAIRS AND ORGANIZATIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF CHILDREN'S SERVICES COUNCIL (CSC) OF BROWARD COUNTY (BC), KENNETH KING, explained that they were a statutorily authorized special district which was founded 25 years ago where their only funding was through property tax and that their millage was currently 0.45. He highlighted how CSC impacted Margate and that in fiscal year 2024/25, they serviced over 4,000 residents and that $3,500,000 was spent in the City. He described that the services their constituents received ranged from swimming lessons to food mitigation programs and family support. He welcomed questions.
COMMISSIONER, ARLENE R. SCHWARTZ, assumed that the reason Mr. King was in attendance was to explain to the public of the unintended consequences of voting “yes” to reduce homestead as it would remove the funding for CSC.
DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC AFFAIRS AND ORGANIZATIONAL DEVELOPMENT OF CSC OF BC, KING, concurred with Commissioner Schwartz and advised that the Amendment 3 impact would be a cut of $15,000,000 in the first year, $30,000,000 in the second year and thereafter, it would probably be based on what was presented and that 37% - 40% of their budget would be consistently reduced.
Discussion ensued.
VICE MAYOR, ANTHONY N. CAGGIANO, thanked CSC for what they did and hoped that Amendment 3 would not pass.
Discussion ensued.
COMMISSIONER, JOANNE SIMONE, thanked CSC for what they did and asked if they still offered their free book program.
DIRECTOR OF PUBLIC AFFAIRS AND ORGANIZATIONAL DEVELOPMENT CSC OF BC, KING, explained that they still have their book program which had been expanded.
Discussion ensued including on how to receive free books.
